title: Retries, decorators and function identity
question: Why is a wrapper not the same thing as the operation it wraps?

steps.title: The caller invokes one logical operation
steps.narration: The caller names fetch_weather. A decorator can wrap that callable without being the application itself.

steps.title: First response is 503 in this selected scenario
steps.narration: This synthetic response selects the transient-failure branch. It does not prove every 503 is absorbed or every request should retry.

after.name: decision
after.value: Check idempotency, retry policy and remaining deadline

steps.title: Repeat the same request edge with a new attempt
steps.narration: The same participant and connection IDs are used again. The frame is another authored attempt, not another API or a new observed run.

steps.title: This branch succeeds; another branch can exhaust retries
steps.narration: 200 is the selected success case. A separate failure walkthrough must explain deadline expiry, exhausted attempts and error propagation.
questions: What if the operation already wrote data before the timeout?
Where is the final error recorded?

steps.title: wraps preserves metadata, not retry correctness
steps.narration: functools.wraps copies metadata and exposes the wrapped callable for introspection. It does not implement retries, guarantee every logger name or configure an orchestrator task ID.
steps.takeaway: Separate operation identity, wrapper policy, framework task identity and observed attempt.
